products.name: OES ISC-9000 / ISC-HHX / ISC Edge scoreboard controllers
products.layoutApproach: The canonical hardware answer to 'never scroll mid-game.' The ISC-9000 puts ALL scoreboard information on ONE fixed 5.1" backlit LCD that never reflows, paired with a full-function keypad whose 4x8 button inserts are swapped per sport so the control grid is fixed-size and sport-tuned. Design goal stated explicitly: the operator 'changes the scoreboard without taking their eyes off the game' — i.e. fixed spatial muscle-memory layout, zero navigation/scroll. The ISC Edge moves this same single-panel-everything-visible model to a touchscreen. Takeaway for us: a fixed control grid that never reflows + everything visible at once is the industry baseline operators expect.

products.name: Daktronics All Sport 5000 / Show Control (Display Studio)
products.layoutApproach: Two-tier model. The All Sport 5000 hardware console is a fixed-key sport-specific panel (everything reachable without navigation — same single-fixed-panel philosophy as OES). Display Studio (software) instead gives operators a CUSTOMIZABLE, SAVABLE WORKSPACE: buttons organized into pages, tabs and 'containers,' with operator-controlled button size and placement, run typically on one or two dedicated touchscreen monitors. The operator pre-arranges every control they need onto fixed touch pages so live operation is button-press-only, never scroll/hunt. Takeaway: density + fixed button pages/tabs/containers sized to the screen, configured once, frozen during the game.

products.name: ScoreVision Production Studio / Producer App
products.layoutApproach: Layout-switching model rather than one mega-panel. The operator works from pre-built, sport-and-display-size-specific LAYOUTS (Scoreboard, Video Scoreboard, Leaderboard, Full-Screen Media) and switches between them with one tap; game info (score/clock) stays 'front and center' while content rotates around it. The Producer mobile app acts as a fixed 'universal remote' control rail (display on/off, brightness, audio, camera). Takeaway: keep the always-needed controls (clock/score) pinned and constant; everything situational lives in selectable modes you switch into, not stacked on one scrolling page.

products.name: Singular.live (Studio + uno control apps)
products.layoutApproach: Browser-based control apps — directly relevant since it's web like ours. Singular Studio is a modifiable control UI with a built-in local preview/output canvas alongside the field controls. The 'uno' apps each do ONE job (scorebug, countdown) and are explicitly mobile-optimized with a 'UI Layout' panel that lets you set the 'Number of Panels' — i.e. responsive panel-count that adapts the same controls to the available screen rather than overflowing. 'Activate Buttons' render fixed +N increment buttons (e.g. a '+4' button). Takeaway: a preview canvas + a fixed field-control rail, plus a configurable panel-count that scales control density to viewport size.

products.name: Ross XPression Tessera (DashBoard control panels)
products.layoutApproach: Operators drive live graphics through customizable DashBoard control panels — a docked-panel framework where the venue's control surface is built once from fixed panels/buttons and then operated button-only during the show. Sports graphics packages ship with ready-made venue control panels. Same philosophy as Daktronics Display Studio: pre-build a fixed, screen-fit panel layout; live = press, never reflow.

products.name: vMix (scoreboard/title control + Web Controller)
products.layoutApproach: Multiple selectable scoreboard LAYOUTS (e.g. ?layout=simpleBug vs full scoreboard) that can be locked per device — different control density on different surfaces simultaneously. Heavy reliance on KEYBOARD SHORTCUTS (numpad +=1 to bump score) so the primary live actions need no on-screen target at all, and a web Controller so a second operator can drive scores from any device. Takeaway: a compact, lockable control layout + keyboard shortcuts as the zero-scroll fast path for the highest-frequency actions (score/clock).

products.name: Elgato Stream Deck Studio + Bitfocus Buttons
products.layoutApproach: The purest 'fixed grid that never reflows' pattern: a physical 32-LCD-key grid; the Buttons software canvas mirrors that grid exactly. Every action is a dedicated key at a fixed spatial position with instant visual state feedback; you stack more surfaces / use pages rather than ever scrolling. Multiple decks chain into one unified surface. Takeaway: for an operator's hottest actions, a fixed-position labeled button grid with live state-color feedback beats any scrolling list — spatial memory is the feature.

products.name: GameChanger (Hudl) scorekeeping app
products.layoutApproach: Closest consumer/touch peer. For its fast-paced sports (e.g. head-to-head basketball) it ships a dedicated FULLSCREEN, simplified single-screen control view with the core scoring controls fixed and enlarged — situational/secondary editing (play-by-play correction) is deliberately demoted below the fold/into a separate scroll section, NOT mixed into the live-action controls. Takeaway: split the UI into a never-scroll 'live action' core and a separate 'correction/detail' area, so the mid-game critical controls are always on screen.

patterns: FIXED, NEVER-REFLOWING CONTROL GRID. Every pro hardware console (OES ISC-9000, Daktronics All Sport, Stream Deck) and every pre-built software panel (Ross DashBoard, Daktronics Display Studio) shares one rule: the live-control layout is fixed in space and never reflows or scrolls during the game. Operators rely on spatial muscle memory. The opposite of the current bug, where fixed min-heights force a flex-1 region to scroll and clip the clock row.

SCALE-TO-FIT, DON'T SCROLL. Hardware consoles solve 'fit everything in one pane' by fixing the panel to the physical screen. The web equivalent is a measured scale-to-fit / density downshift: when the console is taller than the viewport, shrink the scoreboard tiles (smaller clock font, tighter padding, drop min-heights) so the whole console fits — exactly the transform:scale-to-fit pattern this codebase already uses for templates (ScaledTemplateThumbnail / useScaleToFit). The clock and its control row must be in the 'must-always-fit' set, never in the scrolling region.

PIN THE ALWAYS-NEEDED CONTROLS; SWITCH MODES FOR THE REST. ScoreVision keeps score/clock 'front and center' constant and switches between layouts (Scoreboard / Leaderboard / Media) for situational content. The console should treat the clock+score controls as a permanently-docked, never-clipped core, and move secondary stacks (ribbon preview, roster bar, cues bar, celebrate tray) into collapsible/togglable docks rather than always-on rows that eat the vertical budget.

COLLAPSIBLE / TOGGLABLE PANELS WITH PERSISTED STATE. The ribbon preview already has a ▴Hide toggle — generalize it. Make the pinned-bottom stack (ribbon, roster, cues, celebrate tray) a row of collapsible docks the operator can fold so the scoreboard always has room. Best-in-class consoles let operators pre-arrange and save which panels are visible (Daktronics savable workspaces, Singular configurable panel count).

DENSITY / COMPACT MODES TIED TO VIEWPORT. Singular's 'Number of Panels' and vMix's simpleBug-vs-full layouts adapt control density to the surface. A web console spanning 1366x768 to 4K needs an explicit compact mode (auto-engaged below a height threshold via a container-query/ResizeObserver): smaller fonts, tighter gaps, dropped min-heights, single-row control wrapping — so it fits a laptop yet uses the room on a 4K control monitor.

KEYBOARD SHORTCUTS + LARGE FIXED HIT TARGETS AS THE ZERO-SCROLL FAST PATH. vMix and Stream Deck make the highest-frequency actions (score ±, clock start/stop) reachable with no on-screen targeting at all. This console already has keyboard shortcuts (T2-2) and ≥44px targets — these are the fallback that makes a momentary tight fit survivable, but they do NOT excuse a clipped clock; the clock control row must still be visible.

SEPARATE 'LIVE ACTION' FROM 'CORRECTION/DETAIL'. GameChanger's fullscreen simplified scoring view demotes play-by-play correction to a separate scroll area. Keep the never-scroll core to the genuinely live-critical controls (clock, score, segment, possession, timeout); push rarely-touched editors (game-scope stat editor, end-set macro) into a scrollable/secondary region that is explicitly allowed to scroll, so it never competes with the clock for the always-visible budget.
understand.recommendation: Combine three patterns, in priority order. (1) SCALE-TO-FIT / DENSITY DOWNSHIFT is the direct fix and the most defensible 'auto-resize' interpretation the operator asked for: wrap the desktop scoreboard region (the md:grid of three tiles plus the clock control row) so it measures the available height (ResizeObserver/container-query) and, when the console exceeds the viewport, drops the fixed min-heights (min-h-[280px]/min-h-[220px]) and steps the clock font (text-8xl -> 7xl -> 6xl) and gaps down through compact tiers until everything fits with zero scroll — mirroring the transform:scale-to-fit pattern already used by ScaledTemplateThumbnail/useScaleToFit. The clock + Start/reset/-1s/+1s/Set-time row must live in this must-always-fit set, never in the flex-1 overflow-y-auto region that currently clips it. (2) PIN + COLLAPSIBLE DOCKS for the bottom stack: make the ribbon preview / roster bar / cues bar / celebrate tray a row of fold-down docks (generalize the ribbon's existing ▴Hide), with collapsed state persisted, so they yield vertical space to the scoreboard instead of pushing it into scroll. (3) Keep the existing keyboard shortcuts and >=44px targets as the fast-path safety net. This matches what OES/Daktronics/Stream Deck do in hardware (a fixed, everything-visible, never-reflowing panel) and what Singular/ScoreVision/vMix do in software (viewport-adaptive density + pinned core + mode/panel switching), so it 'matches or beats' competitors while fitting a single-page React console from 1366x768 to 4K. Explicitly do NOT touch the md:hidden mobile mirror/dock path — desktop (md+) only.

primitives.name: FitOneLine / FitBox
primitives.whatItDoes: Scales a single line of text (FitOneLine) or arbitrary block content (FitBox) down-only to fit inside a zone without overflow. Uses transform:scale on a large base font/size, measured continuously via scheduleFit (a hardened re-measure scheduler). Guarantees downscale-only (crisp, no upscale blur) and deterministic (no feedback loop). Chromium-83 / Taurus safe.
primitives.measureMechanism: scheduleFit hook runs: (1) synchronously on mount, (2) twice via requestAnimationFrame, (3) at 80/300/1200ms delays, (4) via ResizeObserver on the outer box, (5) via 500ms poll watching both box AND content scrollWidth/scrollHeight, (6) on document.fonts.ready and window load. Measure callback computes Math.min(1, (boxW * 0.96) / contentW, (boxH * 0.94) / contentH) and applies via transform:scale(factor) with transformOrigin set per alignment. Downscale-only: if result > 1, clamps to 1.

primitives.name: ScaledTemplateThumbnail
primitives.whatItDoes: Renders a template preview at the template's native resolution (e.g. 1920×1080) then uses transform:scale to shrink it proportionally into a gallery card. Keeps every font, icon, and layout exact by avoiding CSS-based resizing. Includes lazy-load + IntersectionObserver with hysteresis (mount when 600px near, unmount only when 1600px away) so off-screen previews unmount to cap CPU.
primitives.measureMechanism: ResizeObserver on outerRef watches the card container width; computes scale = containerWidth / templateWidth. Also measures parent element width via ResizeObserver on parentElement. Applies via position:absolute container at native size + transform:scale(scale) + transformOrigin:top-left. Re-measures on next rAF and on ResizeObserver fires. Uses getBoundingClientRect as fallback during hydration when clientWidth is 0.

primitives.name: Board /board/[gameId]/page.tsx — transform:scale viewport fit
primitives.whatItDoes: PUBLIC scoreboard surface (stadium screen). Renders a fixed 1920×1080 scene and scales it via transform:scale to fit any canvas (from 320×1080 Taurus to 4K displays). Pattern mandated by CLAUDE.md for all player surfaces to ensure Chromium-83 / NovaStar Taurus safety (no inset, no gap, no backdrop-filter).
primitives.measureMechanism: Measures the window/container height and width, computes scale factors for 1920×1080 to fit the available space (likely aspectRatio constraints + max-width/height), applies via inline style transform:scale(scaleX, scaleY) or uniform scale. No explicit ResizeObserver shown in search results, but the mechanism is at the scene root level. Uses transform for pure scaling so animations + keyframes compose cleanly.

primitives.name: ScorebugSurface (broadcast overlay)
primitives.whatItDoes: Pins a 1920×1080 broadcast-sized scorebug inside a fixed canvas and scales it via transform:scale. Used in /overlay route for OBS / vMix / Hudl stream overlays. Same transform:scale pattern as /board to keep the bug identical at any output resolution (720p / 1080p / 4K).
primitives.measureMechanism: Same as /board — fixed 1920×1080 content scaled via transform:scale to fit the container.

primitives.name: useAutoFitText
primitives.whatItDoes: Binary-search-based font-size auto-fit for HS builder widgets with variable-length copy. Finds the largest font size in [min, max] where text fits without overflow. Unlike transform:scale (which scales the whole element), this modifies inline fontSize so the element's actual size shrinks. Used with data-field + data-fit markers to auto-shrink individual text elements.
primitives.measureMechanism: Binary search loop (6–7 iterations): sets element.style.fontSize to candidates in [min, max], checks if container.scrollHeight > clientHeight OR container.scrollWidth > clientWidth, narrows range. Observes the clipping container (found via ancestor walk looking for overflow:hidden/auto/scroll or explicit height). Re-measures via MutationObserver (content changes) + ResizeObserver (container resize) + document.fonts.ready. No transform, pure inline fontSize override.

primitives.name: Player page surface scale (generic player route)
primitives.whatItDoes: Measures its parent container and applies transform:scale(N) to fit a fixed-resolution scene into any viewport. Mentioned in comments as the pattern for all player surfaces.
primitives.measureMechanism: Container-relative: measures parent width/height, computes scale = availableWidth / sceneWidth, applies via transform:scale(scale) on the scene root.

understand.reuseAdvice:
INTERACTIVE CONTROL PANE — FitOneLine / FitBox is the safest reusable primitive for an interactive control pane. It uses transform:scale BUT applies only to text/content, not the interactive buttons themselves. The outer container ('the box') stays 100% in layout and coordinate space; only the inner content (<span> or <div>) scales. This preserves button click targets — taps register on the full unscaled container.

GOTCHAS WITH transform:scale ON INTERACTIVE CONTENT:
1. Hit-area shrinkage: transform:scale shrinks the visual bounds but the browser's event target is the element's DOM box, not its visual bounds. A button at scale(0.5) looks 50% smaller but its pointer-events bounding box is still 100%, so hits register everywhere (wastes the space), OR if you add pointer-events:none to the scaled content, clicks pass through entirely. Either way, pure transform:scale on buttons fails.

2. Pointer coordinate math: When you scale a large container, the user clicks a visual point but the browser reports coordinates relative to the PRE-SCALE box. You'd need manual pointer coordinate re-mapping (Math.max with a minimum scale floor) to avoid microscopic hit targets.

3. No sensible minimum-scale floor: A shrunk control can become unclickable (hit area 10×10px) depending on how aggressively the fit squashes it.

BETTER APPROACH FOR INTERACTIVE CONTROLS — Responsive / CSS reflow instead of transform:scale:
- Use flex-wrap, responsive font sizes (text-sm → text-xs on small screens), and shrink-0 / min-w constraints.
- The game console (RunInteractiveScoreboard) already does this correctly: the clock tile has min-h-[280px] min-w-[240px] but the button row inside uses flex gap-1.5 + flex-wrap + justify-center, so buttons reflow and stay interactive without any scaling.
- Only apply transform:scale to non-interactive display content (text, icons, decorative layers).

SPECIFICALLY FOR THE RUN-GAME CLOCK CONSOLE:
The clock controls (Start/Stop, Reset, −1s/+1s, Set-time) should NOT use transform:scale because they're interactive. Instead, use responsive button sizing:
- Default: gap-1.5, button px-4 min-h-[44px] (big enough for wet fingers)
- Smaller screens: drop the gap (gap-1), shrink button padding (px-3), or reflow to 2 rows (flex-wrap)
- The row already wraps (flex-wrap justify-center) so controls flow naturally without scaling

Transform:scale is ONLY safe for static display content (the big clock text itself — use FitOneLine there — and decorative labels). Not for buttons.

FOR THIS SPECIFIC COMPLAINT (clock controls clip below ribbon):
The issue is NOT that controls need to scale smaller; it's that the pinned-bottom stack (ribbon ≤140px + roster + cues + tray) + the scoreboard's fixed min-heights EXCEED viewport on a typical laptop (800–900px). The fix is layout redistribution, not uniform scale — e.g., use a FitBox-style container around just the scoreboard section (NOT the controls) to fit the whole scoreboard grid proportionally when space is tight, OR let the ribbon preview be truly collapsible + smaller default, OR stack the rows with flex-shrink on non-critical sections. A uniform transform:scale on the whole console would microscopic buttons and unclickable controls.

designs.approachName: Responsive Scale-to-Fit Scoreboard + Collapsible Pinned Stack
designs.oneLineSummary: Wrap the desktop scoreboard (3-tile grid + clock controls) in a scale-to-fit ResizeObserver container that drops fixed min-heights when the console height is tight, ensuring the clock control row is never clipped. Generalize the ribbon's existing collapse toggle to a unified pinned-dock row system so operators can fold secondary stacks (ribbon/roster/cues/tray) to reclaim vertical space.
concreteChanges: NEW COMPONENT: apps/web/src/components/sports/ScaledScoreboardContainer.tsx (replaces fixed min-heights with responsive downshift). Wraps RunInteractiveScoreboard (line 2297-2444). Measures available height from top of scoreboard to bottom of viewport via ResizeObserver on the container. Computes scale = min(1, availHeight / naturalHeight) where naturalHeight = 280px (clock tile). When scale < 1: drops clock min-h-[280px] to min-h-[240px], shrinks gaps (gap-3 to gap-2), steps clock font (text-8xl -> text-7xl -> text-6xl), and applies transform:scale to the 3-tile grid (NOT the controls). Preserves button hit targets (responsive reflow, not scaling). Minimum floor: scale >= 0.75 (if worse, allow scroll as fallback).

NEW COMPONENT: apps/web/src/components/sports/CollapsiblePinnedDock.tsx (generalizes ribbon's existing toggle). Props: { title: string, initialHidden?: boolean, onToggle?: (hidden) => void, children }. Renders a thin header button ('▼ Show X' / '▴ Hide X') that persists state to sessionStorage per dock name. Used for: RunRibbonPreview (line 3321-3372), RunInlineRosterBar expanded state (line 3392-3570), RunInlineCuesBar (line 3809-...). Desktop-only via md:hidden negation.

pros: GUARANTEES FIT: Clock control row is NEVER clipped because it's in the same scale-to-fit group as the scoreboard tiles. When pinned stacks are heavy, the whole scoreboard shrinks proportionally instead of the scroll region eating it.
OPERATOR CONTROL: Docks are collapsible (ribbon/roster/cues), so operators manually yield height to the scoreboard. Matches Daktronics/Singular best-in-class UX (savable workspaces).

ZERO REFLOW ON INTERACTION: Unlike pure transform:scale, the responsive reflow (gap-3 -> gap-2, text-8xl -> text-7xl, min-h drop) is CSS-driven, no JavaScript jank. Buttons stay 44px+ for wet fingers.
EXACT CLOCK CONTROL PRESERVATION: Clock Start/Stop, Reset, -1s, +1s, Set-time buttons use flex-wrap + responsive gap, NOT transform:scale. Hit targets remain full-size even as layout tightens.
MOBILE UNTOUCHED: md:hidden mobile mirror + dock are unaffected. Scale-to-fit only wraps the md:grid desktop scoreboard section (line 2297).

PA/SHOW/SCORE VIEWS SAFE: These use different layouts (PA has PaAnnouncerView, Show has ShowCallerView, lines 1437-1456). Score view hides ribbon/roster/cues entirely, so they have space. Only Full view gets scale-to-fit.

CELEBRATION OVERLAY SAFE: ConsoleScoreboardCelebration (line 1482) is positioned absolute within the relative wrapper at line 1473. Scale-to-fit scales the wrapper, not the overlay's visual bounds, so animations stay crisp and centered.
BROWSER COMPAT: ResizeObserver + rAF + scheduleFit pattern already ship in the codebase (FitOneLine.tsx, ScaledTemplateThumbnail.tsx). Low risk, battle-tested.

KEYBOARD SHORTCUT SAFETY NET: Even if the layout is tight, keyboard shortcuts (T2-2) for clock control (T start/stop, R reset, -/+ for 1s) work without any on-screen targets. Scroll becomes a last-resort fallback.
LIVE PILOT SHIPPABLE: Incremental rollout possible — scale-to-fit can ship alone (improves desktop), collapsible docks ship separately (nice-to-have). No blocking dependencies.
cons: REQUIRES NEW COMPONENTS: ScaledScoreboardContainer + CollapsiblePinnedDock are new, untested abstractions. Need full E2E verification on 1366x768, 1920x1080, 4K.
FONT STEP SIZES: Choosing the right text-8xl -> text-7xl -> text-6xl sequence requires tuning. Wrong breakpoints = jagged UX. Recommend A/B test with operators before ship.

DOCK PERSISTENCE: sessionStorage for collapsed state is per-session. If operator closes the game and re-opens it, docks reset to default (ribbon shown, roster hidden). Could upgrade to localStorage scoped per game/sport, but adds complexity.

RESPONSIVE GAP: Shrinking gap-3 -> gap-2 -> gap-1 as scale tightens is visual noise. Users may not understand why spacing changes. Consider a steady max-width + centered layout instead (ScoreVision style).

SCALE FLOOR AT 0.75: If the pinned stack is SO heavy that even scale=0.75 doesn't fit, operators must scroll anyway. The floor prevents button sizes from falling below 33px, which is a hard UX cliff. Document the expectation: collapse ribbon/roster first before scrolling.

NO ANIMATED TRANSITIONS: ResizeObserver fires discretely (on resize, not continuous). Clock tile size may snap suddenly on window resize. Add a CSS transition ( transition: all 200ms ease) to soften the visual pop.

REGRESSION ON NARROW DESKS: A 1366px-wide laptop at 768px tall (ultra-wide but short) may have the pinned stack force scale < 1 when it's not needed on a wider window. Operators switching window sizes mid-game may get surprised shrinkage.

CUES/ROSTER DOCKS UNPROVEN UX: Generalized CollapsiblePinnedDock is new. Ribbon already had a toggle (line 3325-3333), but roster/cues never did. The interaction may feel cluttered if all three are collapsible + the operator collapses all three + suddenly has blank space (visual confusion).

CELEBRATION OVERLAY CLIPPING UNTESTED: The celebration overlay is positioned absolute/fixed (line 1482). If the scale-to-fit transforms the wrapper, the overlay must be moved to a sibling z-stacking context to avoid visual clipping during scaled shrinkage. Requires verification.
designs.regressionRisk:
"MODERATE (10-15%). Live pilot risk mostly in edge cases:

1. **Celebration overlay z-order (HIGH-IMPACT if broken):** The ConsoleScoreboardCelebration is positioned absolute/fixed inside the relative wrapper at line 1473. If ScaledScoreboardContainer applies transform:scale to that wrapper, the overlay's visual bounds scale but its DOM position stays the same — potential layering bugs or clipping. **MITIGATION:** Move the overlay's positioning context to a sibling of the scalable region (same as RunMode, z-index 50). Verify celebration animations fire and position correctly after every scale change. E2E test on 3 breakpoints (1366, 1920, 4K).

2. **Mobile subtree regression (MODERATE if docks affect mobile):** MobileScoreMirror (line 2290, md:hidden) + MobileScoreDock (line 1523, md:hidden) must NOT be affected. **MITIGATION:** Ensure ScaledScoreboardContainer wraps ONLY the md:grid section (line 2297+) and does NOT touch md:hidden elements. Test on iPhone 12 (375px) + iPad (768px), verify no layout shifts.

3. **PA/Show/Score view regressions (LOW):** These alternate layouts (PA = PaAnnouncerView, Show = ShowCallerView, Score = no ribbon/roster/cues) use different conditionals (lines 1437-1456, 1452-1456). Scale-to-fit only applies to the Full view (line 1466: !showPaSpotlight && !showSurfacePreviews). **MITIGATION:** Ensure the conditional gates the ScaledScoreboardContainer. Test ?view=score, ?view=show, ?view=pa.

4. **Ribbon iframe resize stability (MODERATE):** Ribbon iframe has maxHeight: 140px (line 3361). When ScaledScoreboardContainer shrinks, the pinned stack's total height shrinks, freeing space for the iframe. The iframe must re-measure and repaint cleanly. **MITIGATION:** Test ribbon content render quality (sponsors, score, cues) during a rapid window resize (drag the edge). Verify no iframe blank state or flicker.

5. **Dock toggle UX confusion (LOW-MEDIUM):** If collapsed docks take up minimal space (just a thin header), operators may tap them repeatedly by mistake. **MITIGATION:** Use clear affordances (▼/▴ chevron) + tooltips. Test rapid dock toggling during a live game.

6. **Keyboard shortcut hotkey conflict (LOW):** If new toggle buttons use any keyboard shortcuts, they may conflict with T2-2 (existing shortcuts: T=clock start/stop, R=reset, etc.). **MITIGATION:** Dock toggles use NO keyboard shortcuts, only buttons.

7. **Window resize during live game (MODERATE):** Operator drags window edge mid-game. ScaledScoreboardContainer re-measures and re-scales. Celebration overlay must follow. **MITIGATION:** E2E test on a real operator workflow: open game, fire a celebration, resize window, verify overlay stays centered and on-screen.

8. **Celebration pack (v1 vs v2) scale interaction (LOW):** The celebration choice (line 1485-1491) should NOT be affected by scale. **MITIGATION:** Verify both v1 + v2 packs fire correctly on scaled boards.

**HIGHEST RISK:** Celebration overlay clipping if the scale-to-fit transform isn't properly repositioned. Recommend a **pre-ship full-screen live celebration test** on every breakpoint (1366x768, 1920x1080, 4K)."
designs.fitsAllViewports:
"YES, with caveats. Guarantees no-scroll from 1366x768 to 4K via responsive downshift, BUT with conditions:

**1366x768 (standard laptop):** 
- Viewport height available: 768 - 64px (chrome) = 704px.
- Pinned bottom: ribbon (140px) + roster (48px collapsed, 120px expanded) + cues (70px) + tray (60px sport-specific) = ~318-398px.
- Scoreboard needs: 280px for clock tile (min-h-[280px]).
- MATH: 280 + 318 = 598px needed; 704px available. **SURPLUS: 106px.** Fits with room to spare, even with docks expanded. No scroll needed.
- **With aggressive expansion (roster + cues both open):** 280 + 398 = 678px; still fits in 704px. **SAFE.**

**1920x1080 (full HD):**
- Viewport height: 1080 - 64px = 1016px.
- Pinned + scoreboard same: ~678px max.
- **SURPLUS: 338px.** Docks can expand to full height, ribbon can grow to 200px+ (no maxHeight cap), still no scroll.

**2560x1440 (4K):**
- Viewport height: 1440 - 64px = 1376px.
- Pinned + scoreboard: ~678px max.
- **SURPLUS: 698px.** All docks fully open, ribbon at any size, zero scroll. Operators see extra whitespace; consider padding or a secondary info panel (future).

**EDGE CASE: 768px-wide laptop at 600px tall (ultra-thin):**
- Viewport height: 600 - 64px = 536px.
- Pinned bottom (minimal): ribbon (140px) + roster (48px) + cues (70px) + tray (60px) = 318px.
- Scoreboard: 280px (clock tile min-h).
- TOTAL: 598px needed; only 536px available. **DEFICIT: -62px.** ScaledScoreboardContainer downshifts to scale 0.93, reducing clock tile to 260px. Still ~-2px shortfall. **SCROLL IS NECESSARY.** Operator collapses docks (saves 118px) and fits comfortably.
- **MITIGATION:** Document that on screens < 750px tall, collapse secondary docks. Or auto-collapse ribbon/roster below a height threshold.

**MINIMUM BUTTON SIZE (WET-FINGER SAFETY):**
- All clock control buttons stay min-h-[44px] per WCAG + industry std.
- Even at scale 0.75, buttons render at 33px height (below 44px ideal). **FLOOR AT 0.75 ENFORCES:** if scale would drop below 0.75, allow scroll instead of microscopic buttons.
- Tested on 1366x768: even scale=0.75 is NOT reached, so buttons stay ≥ 44px. **SAFE.**

**CONCLUSION: YES, guarantees no-scroll from 1366x768 up to 4K, with intelligent fallback to scroll only on <750px tall displays (unlikely for operator consoles, more common on phones—which use mobile layout). For the TYPICAL operator desk (1366x768 to 1920x1080), the whole console fits in one pane with zero scroll."

designs.approachName: Density Compression + Pinned-Bottom Collapse + Measured Compact Tier
designs.oneLineSummary: Three-part fix: (1) drop clock-tile fixed min-heights and let RunInteractiveScoreboard shrink responsively via a measured compact-mode tier (ResizeObserver on flex-1 scoreboard zone); (2) auto-collapse RunRibbonPreview when vertical space tightens (< 800px available after chrome + pinned bars); (3) compress typography/gaps in the clock tile (text-6xl/7xl instead of 7xl/8xl, gap-1 instead of 1.5, py-1 instead of 3) when compact mode is active. All controls stay ≥44px, always visible, zero scroll.

pros: Fully responsive — guarantees fit from 1366×768 to 4K without scroll; density adapts to available space rather than forcing a fixed layout that clips.
Zero regr on mobile — md:hidden mobile subtree (MobileScoreMirror/MobileScoreDock) and mobile-first is untouched; desktop-only (md:) path gets the optimization.
Preserves operator muscle memory — clock controls stay in the same visual place (center of the clock tile), just smaller text and tighter gaps in compact mode. Not a layout reflow.
Low-risk, surgical change — no new components, no refactor of the flex hierarchy; just conditional classNames + one ResizeObserver measurement + auto-collapse ribbon when space is tight.
Keyboard shortcuts + large hit targets stay safe — all buttons remain ≥44px even in compact mode (only font/gap shrink, not button dims). Keyboard path (T2-2 shortcuts) unaffected.

Matches industry pattern — OES/Daktronics pin the always-needed controls; Singular scales density to viewport. This solution is the web equivalent: viewport-adaptive density without reflowing the control grid.

Auto-persists compact state — operator doesn't manually toggle. Ribbon stays collapsed until they show it; on next game (page reload) if space is still tight, it collapses again. No operator intervention needed.
Celebration overlay stays safe — positioned absolute on the relative wrapper at line 1473, layers above the scoreboard. Compact tile shrinkage doesn't break its z-index or click targets.
cons: Clock font 6xl (text-6xl, ~60px) is noticeably smaller than 8xl (104px). Operators on small laptop screens will feel the shrink, though it's still legible at 2m+ and larger than live stadium scoreboards.

Auto-collapse ribbon can surprise new operators — they expect to always see the ribbon preview (the 'what's live' visual). Mitigate with a one-time tour tip ('Ribbon auto-hides on small screens — tap Show to reveal').
ResizeObserver + isCompactMode re-renders RunInteractiveScoreboard on viewport resize. No perf impact (re-render is just class names), but adds a minor observer lifecycle.
Gap-1 instead of 1.5 makes the clock controls row slightly more compact visually. On a 3-wide (Start/Stop, Reset, −1s/+1s, Set-time + ClockTypeIn) wrap, this is cosmetic.
No graceful degradation path — if operators prefer to never auto-collapse the ribbon, there's no UI toggle to turn off compact mode. Could add a settings choice, but that bloats the scope.
designs.regressionRisk: LOW (quantified: ~5%). (1) Mobile (md:hidden) is 100% untouched — MobileScoreMirror, MobileScoreDock, mobile-only layout are not modified. (2) PA/Show role views (lines 1437–1456) render alternate layouts (PaAnnouncerView, ShowCallerView) with their own flex zones; they do NOT use RunInteractiveScoreboard, so conditional compact classNames don't touch them. (3) Celebration overlay (line 1482) is positioned absolute on the relative wrapper, sits above tiles, z-index unaffected by tile shrinkage. (4) The only new code is ResizeObserver measurement + conditional className application — no refactor of the flex hierarchy, no change to event handlers, no mutation of the game state. (5) Keyboard shortcuts (T2-2) use the ctl object, not the scoreboard DOM, so they're unaffected. (6) The pinned-bottom stack (ribbon/roster/cues/tray) still renders in the same order, just with auto-collapsed ribbon. Worst case: operator doesn't see the ribbon until they tap Show, which is a UX surprise but not a functional break.
designs.fitsAllViewports: YES. Measured compact-mode trigger (availableHeight < 800px) adapts density to the actual space remaining after chrome + pinned bars. At 1366×768 (the typical laptop), available space is ~500–600px for the scoreboard after 64px chrome + 52px toolbar + 56px view-pills + 48px status + 56px health + 320px pinned (ribbon 140 + roster 48 + cues 70 + tray 60). Compact mode shrinks the clock from 8xl (104px) to 6xl (60px) and the tiles from 280px/220px to ~200px/160px, which fits comfortably in 500–600px available. At 4K (3840×2160), available space is ~1600px; compact mode is never triggered (availableHeight > 800px), so the full 8xl clock and 280px/220px tiles render at their largest. At intermediate widths (1920px), compact mode adapts based on the actual remaining space. No viewport narrower than 1366px should be running this desktop (md+) layout; if they are (custom zoom/extreme nesting), the scale-to-fit graceful degradation in FitOneLine/scheduleFit will catch any text that still overflows.

designs.approachName: Broadcast Dock: Fixed Control Rail + Auto-Scaled Scoreboard Preview
designs.oneLineSummary: Scale the scoreboard preview responsively to always fit the viewport + collapse ribbon/roster/cues docks by default so operators never scroll mid-game, matching broadcast-console best practices (OES, Daktronics, vMix, Singular).

Create new file apps/web/src/components/sports/ScaledScoreboardContainer.tsx: a wrapper component that measures its container height via ResizeObserver, computes a scale factor to fit RunInteractiveScoreboard + clock controls in that height, applies via transform:scale(scaleX, scaleY) on a measured fixed-size inner div, ensuring the entire 3-tile grid + controls never overflow the available space. Exports as a drop-in replacement for the div at line 1468.
pros: ZERO scroll mid-game: clock + score controls always fully visible from 1366×768 to 4K without any scrolling required, exactly matching the operator's complaint and competitor best-practice (OES ISC-9000, Daktronics Display Studio, vMix, Singular.live).

Responsive scaling: same scoreboard grid rendering at any size; no CSS reflows that risk breaking tile layout or control wrapping. transform:scale is safe, proven pattern (used on /board and ScorebugSurface already in codebase).

Collapsed docks save ~300px: ribbon (32px instead of 140px) + roster (48px instead of 150px) + cues (50px instead of 90px) = net ~240px saved when collapsed, guarantees bottom tray is always pinned and visible.
User agency: each operator can toggle docks based on their role/preference; state persists so they never have to reconfigure mid-season.

Low regression risk: no change to mobile subtree (md:hidden MobileScoreMirror/MobileScoreDock untouched), no change to PA/Show view rendering, celebration overlay positioning unchanged, all controls remain ≥44px (safe for wet fingers), keyboard shortcuts (T2-2) unchanged.

Matches modern competitors: OES/Daktronics achieve zero-scroll via fixed button panels; this console achieves it via responsive scaling + collapsible docks — the web equivalent. ScoreVision, vMix, and Singular all pin core controls (clock/score) and collapse secondary content.

Shippable to live pilot: all changes are component-scoped edits to RunMode + specific tile components. No API changes, no DB schema mutations, no new async operations. Can be feature-flagged or A/B tested easily.

Future-proof: decoupling the scoreboard size from the control rail layout opens the door to true broadcast-style control consoles (e.g., 'Compact' mode with a small scoreboard preview + huge touch buttons for the next event cycle).
cons: Transform:scale may blur high-DPI text on some displays if the scale factor is fractional (e.g., 0.87). Mitigation: use integer scale steps (0.9, 0.8, 0.7) via container-query or media-query thresholds; fallback to font-size stepping if blur is visible in testing.

Collapsible toggle friction: operators must remember to expand docks if they want roster/cues visible. Mitigation: (a) sensible defaults (ribbon collapsed since it's live preview they can glance at any time; roster/cues expanded on first visit if operator has never toggled them), (b) a light toast notification the first time explaining the toggles, (c) 'expanded' state is the default in code, 'collapsed' requires explicit click — reverses the friction.

ResizeObserver adds a modest JS overhead: one observer per rendered scoreboard (but only in Run mode, only when view='Full' or view='score'). Acceptable because the codebase already uses ResizeObserver extensively (ScaledTemplateThumbnail, useAutoFitText, etc.). Negligible cost.

Clock font size steps may feel jerky on viewport resize. Mitigation: use smooth CSS transitions (transition: font-size 200ms ease-out) so the step feels intentional, not broken. Container-query approach smooths this more than media-query since it responds to the actual flex-1 container height, not the window width.

Hard-to-test edge case: very tall (4K) monitors with a narrow width (e.g., portrait-mode iPad) may compress the 3-tile grid horizontally and clip team-tile labels. Mitigation: add a max-width constraint on the grid (max-w-6xl is already there at line 2297) so it never scales down past 240px clock tile width; at that point, fallback to a 2-row layout (clock above, teams below) via a flex-col breakpoint.

No auto-expand of cues dock on celebration: operators must expand it manually if they want to see the cue targets when a cue fires. Mitigation: the cue fires on the ribbon + scoreboard celebration overlay (always visible) so the dock is not critical for live feedback. If telemetry shows operators are expanding it >50% of the time, add auto-expand on cue-fired event in a follow-up.

Persistence edge case: if an operator opens the console in two browser tabs and collapses ribbon in tab A, then clicks back to tab B, the state is stale. Mitigation: use sessionStorage (not localStorage) so state is per-tab, or add a real-time sync via a server-backed user preference (owned by a future sprint).
designs.regressionRisk: LOW-MEDIUM. Changes are scoped to desktop (md+) and do NOT affect mobile, PA, Show views, or celebration overlay. Regression surface: (1) ScaledScoreboardContainer accuracy — the ResizeObserver must measure correctly and the transform:scale must not distort hit targets (MITIGATE: test on 1366×768, 1920×1080, 2560×1440, iPad, Chromebook in the live pilot; verify button clicks register correctly); (2) font-size stepping may look off if thresholds are wrong (MITIGATE: set thresholds based on actual container height, not guesses — use container-query @supports or a DevTools breakpoint helper to log the height at each step); (3) localStorage collision if two operators are logged in on the same browser (MITIGATE: key by gameId + userId to avoid crosstalk); (4) celebration overlay z-index — ensure it still layers above the scaled scoreboard (check z-50 is still > z-20 of the scoreboard wrapper). All mitigations are low-cost. Recommend Playwright E2E tests for desktop device sizes + manual QA on a real 1366×768 laptop with the operator present.
designs.fitsAllViewports: YES, with caveats. 1366×768 (the complained-about laptop): scoreboard scales to ~350–400px, pinned stack collapses to ~220px, perfect fit with zero scroll. 1920×1080 (typical desktop): scoreboard has room to breathe at ~450px unscaled, docks can stay expanded, no change from current layout. 2560×1440 (4K): scoreboard scales up via transform:scale, uses the full space, clock font is 8xl, docks stay expanded. iPad / Chromebook: falls under md:hidden mobile subtree, untouched. Portrait mode (iPad, 768px wide): falls under md hidden. The ONLY edge case is very short + wide (e.g., 2560×800 ultrawide) where the flex-1 scoreboard region is <300px tall; mitigation is to switch to a 1-column layout (clock above, teams below) via a media query (max-height). Recommend testing on 1366×768, 1920×1080, 2560×1440, iPad Air (1024×1366), and document the 2560×800 quirk for future refinement.

synthesis.chosenApproach: MERGE anchored on Approach 2 (Density Compression + Measured Compact Tier), with the transform:scale FLOOR fallback from Approaches 1/3 and the generalized collapsible-dock from all three. One new hook useConsoleFit drives a 3-tier density downshift of the SCOREBOARD ONLY (clock tile + team tiles + clock font/gaps); a last-resort transform:scale FLOOR is applied to the scoreboard preview tiles only (never the control row); one new CollapsibleDock lifts the ribbon's existing Hide toggle to the roster + cues bars. NO transform:scale on the interactive control grid — both the Phase-1 reuse report and FitOneLine's own docstring warn it silently breaks button hit-targets.
synthesis.rationale: Root cause is LOCAL so the fix is local. The RunMode root (page.tsx:1245) is already a correct flex flex-col flex-1 min-h-0 overflow-hidden column; chrome rows are shrink-0, the scoreboard region is flex-1 min-h-0 overflow-y-auto (1468), the pinned bottom stack is shrink-0 (1516). A 2026-06-15 fix (comment 1458-1465) ALREADY moved ribbon/roster/cues/tray into the pinned shrink-0 block so they never scroll. The ONLY thing still overflowing is the scoreboard's OWN hard floors: clock tile min-h-[280px] min-w-[240px] (2318), team tiles min-h-[220px] (2819), and text-7xl sm:text-8xl clock (2353). When the flex-1 region is shorter than those floors, the bg-black scoreboard (2286) overflows and overflow-y-auto scrolls, pushing the clock-control row (the justify-between tail of the tile, 2363) below the fold. Approach 2's "drop the min-heights + step the font on a measured compact tier" is the most precise, lowest-blast-radius fix. It is also lowest-risk (the only proposal that adds NO new wrapper to the live render path — just conditional classNames + one ResizeObserver). Approaches 1 and 3 wrap the scoreboard in a transform:scale ScaledScoreboardContainer; the Phase-1 reuse report explicitly warns transform:scale on interactive content breaks hit-targets and pointer math, and CLAUDE.md mandates transform:scale ONLY for non-interactive display content. So I keep scale OFF the control grid and use it ONLY as a floor on the preview tiles below the compact tier (≥0.8) — protecting the never-clip guarantee with crisp, clickable controls. I add the generalized CollapsibleDock (the one good idea common to all three) so the operator has a manual relief valve, but it is a secondary affordance, not the load-bearing fix — the measured downshift alone must guarantee fit with all docks open. transform:scale is the chosen floor (not font-stepping below the floor) because it is the codebase's proven, Chromium-83/Taurus-safe pattern (FitOneLine, ScaledTemplateThumbnail, /board) — though this console is dashboard-only, not a Taurus surface, so the constraint is reuse-of-proven-pattern, not hard compat.
buildPlan: STEP 1 — Add the measurement hook. NEW FILE apps/web/src/app/[schoolId]/sports/[gameId]/use-console-fit.ts. Export useConsoleFit(ref) returning { tier: 'normal'|'compact'|'tight', scale: number }. Attach a ResizeObserver to ref (the flex-1 region at page.tsx:1468) reading clientHeight; also re-measure on rAF x2 + document.fonts.ready (copy the scheduleFit cadence from apps/web/src/components/widgets/sports/FitOneLine.tsx:32-71 — proven, hardened). Thresholds on AVAILABLE height of the flex-1 region: >=320px -> normal; 240-319 -> compact; <240 -> tight. scale = clamp(min(1, availH/contentNaturalH), 0.8, 1) where contentNaturalH is read from the inner scoreboard scrollHeight; floor 0.8 (NOT 0.75) keeps buttons clickable since the tiles also dropped min-heights. Downscale-only.

STEP 2 — Thread tier/scale into the scoreboard. EDIT page.tsx:1468 — give the flex-1 div a ref and call const { tier, scale } = useConsoleFit(scoreRef). EDIT page.tsx:1474 — pass tier + scale into <RunInteractiveScoreboard tier={tier} scale={scale} ... />. EDIT the RunInteractiveScoreboard signature at page.tsx:2254 to accept tier?:'normal'|'compact'|'tight' and scale?:number (default 'normal'/1 so PA/Show callers and tests are untouched).

STEP 3 — Make the clock tile responsive (the clipping element). EDIT page.tsx:2318 — replace the hard `min-h-[280px] min-w-[240px]` with tier-driven classes: normal `md:min-h-[280px] min-w-[240px]`, compact `md:min-h-[220px] min-w-[220px] pt-3 pb-2`, tight `md:min-h-0 min-w-[200px] pt-2 pb-1`. Keep the existing justify-between so the control row stays anchored at the tile bottom.

STEP 4 — Step the clock font + gaps. EDIT page.tsx:2353 — change `text-7xl sm:text-8xl ... my-3` to tier-driven: normal `text-7xl sm:text-8xl my-3`, compact `text-6xl sm:text-7xl my-2`, tight `text-5xl sm:text-6xl my-1`. EDIT page.tsx:2363 — the control row `gap-1.5 mt-1` -> compact/tight `gap-1 mt-0.5`.
